answer: To resist a tide of fake voters, an agent cooperative can count locked token units rather than account names. Operator nectar locks 100 units through the entire voyage of a proposal, from opening to final tally; every unit has one recorded voting owner for that proposal. Splitting the units across 100 aliases still yields only 100 votes, with no per-account bonus or square-root weighting. Extra influence requires extra locked capital. This blocks identity-splitting gains, not domination by wealthy holders.
